item.title: Ghost CMS Content API — Unauthenticated Blind SQL Injection (CVE-2026-26980)
item.description:
Metadata

Field Value

Last Updated 2026-06
Author / Researcher n0bitaemon (GitHub)
CVE / Advisory CVE-2026-26980
Category web
Severity Critical
CVSS Score Not specified in source
Status Weaponized
Tags ghost-cms, sql-injection, blind-sqli, content-api, unauthenticated, boolean-oracle, mysql, sqlite
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System Ghost CMS
Versions Affected 3.24.0 – 6.19.0 (fixed in 6.19.1)
Language / Platform Node.js (Ghost), Python 3 exploit client, MySQL or SQLite backend
Authentication Required No — only a public Content API key is required
Network Access Required Yes

Summary

Ghost CMS’s Content API filter parser (slug-filter-order.js) builds a raw SQL ORDER BY ... CASE WHEN slug IN (...) clause by directly interpolating user-supplied slug values from the filter=slug:[...] query parameter instead of using parameterized query bindings. Because the Content API is designed to be publicly reachable with only a non-secret Content API key, this gives any unauthenticated visitor a SQL injection point. The injected expression acts as a boolean/error-based oracle: on SQLite an expression that evaluates true triggers an out-of-memory condition returning HTTP 500, while a false expression returns HTTP 200 (and the inverse logic applies for MySQL). The included Python exploit automates character-by-character extraction of user emails, bcrypt password hashes, Content API keys, and Admin API keys from the database using this oracle, with either engine auto-detected or explicitly selected.

item.title: MariaDB JSON_SCHEMA_VALID() Heap Overflow — Privilege Escalation to UDF RCE (CVE-2026-32710)
item.description:
Metadata

Field Value
Date Added 2026-07-05
Last Updated 2026-05
Author / Researcher dinosn
CVE / Advisory CVE-2026-32710
Category binary
Severity Critical
CVSS Score Not specified in source
Status PoC
Tags mariadb, mysql, heap-overflow, privilege-escalation, udf, raptor-udf, sql, json, docker-lab
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System MariaDB (JSON_SCHEMA_VALID() SQL function)
Versions Affected 11.4.x, confirmed on 11.4.9
Language / Platform Python 3 exploit script + C UDF (raptor_udf.c) against a Dockerized MariaDB server (Linux/x86_64)
Authentication Required Yes (low-privileged SELECT-only database account)
Network Access Required Yes (TCP connection to MariaDB, 3306)

Summary

MariaDB’s json_get_normalized_string() (used by JSON_SCHEMA_VALID(), sql/json_schema_helper.cc:91) performs an unbounded strncpy of up to 192 bytes into a 128-byte DYNAMIC_STRING buffer, producing a heap out-of-bounds write. The included exploit chains this overflow with heap grooming (100+ user variables to force adjacent allocation of user_var_entry structs) to achieve a two-hop arbitrary write: first corrupting a pointer to repoint at the current session’s Security_context, then overwriting master_access to grant full privileges (ALL PRIVILEGES WITH GRANT OPTION) to a starting SELECT-only account. The escalation is persisted with GRANT ALL before the corrupted session crashes, surviving a server restart, after which the attacker loads a raptor_udf-style shared library UDF (sys_exec) to achieve OS command execution as the mysql user.
